messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - CI/CD pipeline failures detected. Multiple GitHub Actions runs failing + GitHub Packages (npm) returning 502s. Alerting on-call and creating thread. Root cause unknown.

alex: seeing a bunch of failing runs that started ~10:12 UTC, all erroring at 'fetching actions/checkout' and package installs error with 502 from npm.pkg.github.com.
maria: confirmed. Builds are stuck on our main hotfix branch (hotfix/urgent-auth-fix). We can't produce artifacts. Customers on the hotfix are waiting.
oncall-engr: I'm on it. Paging SRE. Can someone grab recent deploy logs and a sample failing job id?
sre-lead: grabbing logs now. job id GH-run-78421. Error snippet:```
Error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/org/package - 502 Bad Gateway
at fetchPackage (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/npm/lib/fetch.js:xx:xx)
```

ci-admin: also seeing errors from GitHub Actions self-hosted runner controller: 'unable to connect to GitHub actions service (503)'. Not just packages, Actions API calls are flakey.
devops: checking GitHub status - status.github.com shows partial degradation in Actions + Packages in us-east. pinging GitHub support.
github-status-bot: GitHub status: "Investigating - GitHub Actions and GitHub Packages experiencing degraded performance for some regions." https://www.githubstatus.com/incident/xxxxx
alex: we need a mitigation plan. Hotfix is blocked until we can build/publish. Options: 1) use self-hosted runner to build and push artifacts to S3 and deploy from there, 2) try mirror npm registry (npmjs.org) for the package, 3) roll back to previous release. Thoughts?
maria: hotfix is a security auth token rotation; rollback isn't acceptable for affected customers. Option 1 seems viable: build on self-hosted runner and upload tarball to S3, update deploy to pull from S3. Needs deploy-bot adjustments.
oncall-engr: I can spin up a runner in our VPC and run the workflow locally (semi-manual). Will need someone to change the deploy manifest to point to an S3 tarball URL.
devops: I can prepare a temporary S3 bucket and presigned URLs. We should sign artifacts and record checksums.
deploy-bot: can accept artifact URL via manual trigger:```
/deploy --artifact-url=https://s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp/hotfix-202307.tar.gz --env=prod
```

customer-success: heads up, CS is drafting a message for customers on the affected tenant list. Need ETA estimate and impact statement (which tenants, whether feature degraded).
sre-lead: impact - API gateway is fine, inference runtime unaffected. Only deploy pipelines and new builds blocked. Customers waiting on hotfixes that require new image builds are impacted. Marking customer-impacting: yes. P1 for build-blocking.

alex: action items: 1) oncall-engr to run build on self-hosted runner, 2) devops to create S3 artifact + presigned URL, 3) deploy-bot to accept manual deploy, 4) CI admin to monitor GitHub status and escalate to GitHub support.
oncall-engr: starting build now on runner-03. Will paste logs.
ci-admin: opened ticket with GitHub Support #INC-21345 with attachments of failing job logs and traces. Escalation requested.
maria: if build succeeds, we'll need a quick smoke test checklist. I'll prepare steps.
oncall-engr: build finished locally but package publish step failed (registry unavailable) - skipping publish, created tarball: hotfix-2026-03-15.tar.gz (sha256: abc123...). Uploading to S3 now.
devops: uploaded and generated presigned URL (valid 2 hours): https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp/hotfix-2026-03-15.tar.gz?X-Amz-...

deploy-bot: manual deploy triggered by @alex: /deploy --artifact-url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-temp/hotfix-2026-03-15.tar.gz --env=prod. Starting rollout to 10% canary.
maria: starting smoke tests against canary. auth endpoints, token rotation flow, and metrics checks.
customer-success: prepping message template: "We are currently experiencing CI/CD outages due to GitHub Actions & Packages; deploying hotfixes is delayed. We have a manual mitigation in place and will update customers as we confirm deploy status."
sre-lead: monitoring Datadog - no observability vendor outage on our side, only source-of-truth is GitHub. Also note: our alerting spiked during the initial failures, some noise.
ci-admin: GitHub replied: we've identified an upstream proxy issue affecting Actions and Packages in us-east, mitigation in progress, ETA unknown. We requested priority.

alex: can we run full prod smoke once canary passes? If ok, promote to 100% and notify CS to message customers.
maria: canary is green after 8 minutes. No regressions observed in metrics. Proceeding to 100%.
deploy-bot: promoting rollout to 100% as requested by @maria.
customer-success: messaging sent to affected customers with the manual-mitigation update and expected timeline.

github-status-bot: Update from GitHub: "Partial service recovery for Packages and Actions. Some regions still experiencing errors."
ci-admin: GitHub indicates progressive recovery; they asked to retry publishes. We attempted a test publish and it succeeded for a small private package.
sre-lead: because GitHub is flaky, keep manual artifact path for this hotfix in audit logs. Also add post-incident action: update runbooks to include S3 artifact fallback and an approved manual-deploy checklist.
oncall-engr: confirming final prod verify: all good. Hotfix deployed and serving traffic. Closing mitigation.
alex: good job team. Postmortem action items: 1) document S3 fallback steps and templates, 2) coordinate with GitHub account team for RTO guarantees, 3) update CS playbook for messaging.
customer-success: will follow up with any customers who asked for escalation.
incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved - root cause external (GitHub Actions/Packages outage). Duration: ~55 minutes. Link to incident ticket: INC-2026-0315-07. :white_check_mark:
